domain: Broker recruiting toolkit and per-broker marketing self-service
summary: The prior audit was too generous on both "have" items and too lazy on two "missing" ones. The multi-tenant data model is real at the brokers-table layer but broker IDENTITY resolution runs through three hardcoded email maps in code, and the CRM scoping code FAILS OPEN when that map misses: in app/actions/broker-command-center.ts every scope filter is written `if (scopeToSelf && crmSlug)`, so a broker-role user whose login email is absent from CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL sees every broker's clients and tasks rather than none. The seeded admin_roles emails in the only broker-seeding migration (rebecca.peterson@, paul.stevenson@) do not match the CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL keys (rebeccapeterson@, paul@), which is exactly the shape of input that triggers the fail-open. On the other side, the auditor declared two things "missing" that are built: /admin/broker-links is a genuine per-broker marketing self-service page (per-broker attribution ad links for five landing pages), and /admin/media is a real four-tab browsable asset UI. Both are locked behind superuser-only capability arrays in lib/admin/capabilities.ts ('content.marketing': [], 'content.media': []), not absent. Onboarding is likewise more built than reported: /admin/brokers/new and /admin/crm/settings/team create broker rows and assign admin_roles through UI. The genuinely dark pieces are unchanged and confirmed: marketing-inbox-poll is absent from all 49 vercel.json cron entries despite its own docstring claiming otherwise, producer broker-substitution is inconsistent (build_listing_reveal.py:80 hardcodes Matt's phone, listing_video_v4 has zero agent-resolution code), there is no compliance monitoring of broker email content, and per-broker Instagram publishing does not exist.

items.evidence: lib/data/brokers/getBrokers.ts reads public.brokers with no hardcoded roster and lib/data/types/broker.ts:11-18 confirms BrokerSlug is a permissive string alias precisely because a fixed union drifted — that part of the auditor's claim is real. BUT broker IDENTITY is resolved by three hardcoded code-level maps, not data: lib/admin.ts:2 SUPERUSER_ADMIN_EMAIL='matt@ryan-realty.com'; lib/crm/constants.ts:15-19 CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL hardcodes exactly three login emails; lib/data/brokers/getBrokers.ts:118-119 BROKER_SLUG_ALIASES hardcodes slug aliases (and its own comment says it mirrors a second copy in app/actions/brokers.ts). supabase/migrations/20250312000000_broker_license_and_seed.sql:36-45 seeds admin_roles with 'rebecca.peterson@ryan-realty.com' and 'paul.stevenson@ryan-realty.com' and a comment admitting they are placeholders — neither string is a key in CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor marked this 'have' with 'None at the data-model layer'. That is wrong — the data model is only multi-tenant for DISPLAY. Broker identity resolution is hardcoded in three places, two of them duplicated copies, and adding a fourth broker requires a code deploy, not a DB row. Worse, the mismatch between the migration's placeholder emails and CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL is not cosmetic: it is the exact input that triggers the fail-open scoping bug in the next item.]
items.why_it_matters: Recruiting a fourth broker cannot be done from the admin UI alone — someone must edit and deploy lib/crm/constants.ts, and until they do, that broker's dashboard silently mis-scopes rather than erroring.

items.requirement: Per-broker CRM scoping: brokers log in and see only their own clients, tasks, deals, queue, next steps
items.evidence: The dashboard is real and reachable: app/admin/(protected)/layout.tsx:48-51 admits any admin_roles row (not just superuser), and app/admin/(protected)/broker-dashboard/page.tsx:187-497 renders clients/tasks/deals/needs-action. app/actions/broker-command-center.ts:130 sets scopeToSelf = !isSuperuser || scope==='me'. BUT every scope filter is conditional on a nullable slug and fails OPEN: line 243 `if (scopeToSelf && crmSlug) tasksQuery.eq('assigned_broker', crmSlug)`, line 254 same for the today-count, line 269 same for clientsQuery. crmSlug comes from broker-command-center.ts:124 `CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL[email.toLowerCase()] ?? null` — a broker whose login email is not one of the three hardcoded keys gets crmSlug=null, the .eq() is never applied, and the query returns EVERY broker's clients and tasks. app/actions/crm.ts:1794 repeats the pattern: `if (access.brokerSlug) q = q.eq(...)`, and app/actions/crm.ts:51 sets brokerSlug from the same hardcoded map. Deal scoping has a separate defect: broker-command-center.ts:157-158 filters tc_deals.broker_name against brokers.display_name, which the seed migration sets to 'Rebecca Peterson Ryser' and 'Paul Michael Stevenson' — long legal names unlikely to match how tc_deals.broker_name is written.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor wrote 'None found for this specific requirement — it works and is verified in code across three independent files.' They read the happy path only. The scoping is fail-open, not fail-closed: a broker-role account with an unmapped email is granted a full-book view of every client and task, which for a recruited-broker product is a data-leak class of bug, not a cosmetic one. They also never checked that the tc_deals filter compares display_name to broker_name, where the seeded display names are full legal names and a mismatch silently yields an empty Deals section with no error.]
items.why_it_matters: The pitch to a recruited broker is 'your book, your dashboard.' A fail-open filter breaks the promise in the worst direction, and the deals mismatch makes the dashboard look empty rather than wrong.

items.requirement: Marketing self-service dashboard: any broker sees content created for the brokerage, branded to them
items.evidence: The auditor missed a built surface. app/admin/(protected)/broker-links/page.tsx:11-64 is a real per-broker marketing self-service page: a BROKERS array (matt/rebecca/paul) crossed with five landing pages, emitting per-broker `?agent=<slug>` attribution URLs with copy buttons plus Facebook lead-form routing instructions. It is registered in the nav at lib/admin/nav.ts:189. It is gated by `await requireAdminPage('content.marketing')` (broker-links/page.tsx:30), and lib/admin/capabilities.ts:130 sets `'content.marketing': []` — an empty array meaning superuser-only per that file's own convention (line ~85 comment). So Paul and Rebecca get access-denied on a page written specifically for them. The auditor's other findings hold: broker-dashboard/page.tsx:500-501 hard-gates the Marketing launchpad on `data.isSuperuser`, broker-command-center.ts:283-284 skips the listings read for non-superusers with a matching comment, and app/dashboard/marketing/page.tsx:527-536 gates on any admin_roles row but renders aggregate brain telemetry across 1162 lines with no per-broker filtering.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor said 'missing' and that 'Paul and Rebecca have no marketing surface at all today.' Two surfaces exist and are nav-registered — /admin/broker-links and the Marketing launchpad — both locked by role, not absent. The distinction matters for effort: unlocking broker-links is a one-line change to the CAPABILITY_ROLES array plus a scoping pass so each broker sees only their own row, not an L-sized build. What is genuinely missing is the branded-content half: no page shows a broker brokerage-created creative re-rendered with their name, headshot, or phone.]
items.why_it_matters: Matt's recruiting pitch is the marketing self-service dashboard. Half of the minimum viable version is already written and switched off, which is a much cheaper starting position than the prior audit implied.

items.requirement: Browsable per-broker content/asset library with branded outputs
items.evidence: app/admin/(protected)/media/layout.tsx defines a four-tab media shell (Library, Photo curation, Banners, Stock photos) and app/admin/(protected)/media/page.tsx:8-25 renders AdminMediaManager — a real browsable upload/asset UI, registered in nav at lib/admin/nav.ts:185. media/photos/page.tsx renders a paginated PhotoCurationBoard (48/page, approval + geo + type filters). Access: media/page.tsx:10-11 redirects any non-superuser, and the nav entry requires 'content.media' which lib/admin/capabilities.ts:131 sets to [] (superuser-only). Note media/photos/page.tsx carries NO in-page role check and its parent layout carries none either — a broker who types /admin/media/photos directly gets in, even though nav hides it. The auditor's manifest claim is correct: grep shows data/asset-library/manifest.json is consumed only by lib/pulse-asset-library.ts, lib/blog-hero-images.ts, lib/asset-library.mjs and build-time scripts — no route renders it.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor asserted 'No route under app/ renders this manifest as a browsable gallery' and generalized that to 'No UI exists for a broker to browse'. The first clause is true, the second is false — /admin/media is a browsable gallery UI, it just reads uploaded/curated media rather than the manifest, and it is superuser-gated. Separately they missed an authz inconsistency: /admin/media/photos is nav-hidden but has no page-level gate, so it is reachable by any admin role while its sibling tabs redirect.] Still genuinely missing: any concept of a finished deliverable branded per broker — neither the manifest schema nor the media tables carry a 'branded for broker X' variant.
items.why_it_matters: The evergreen-content-per-broker story needs a gallery of FINISHED branded assets, not a raw-media manager. The shell exists; the branded-variant data model does not.

items.requirement: Content request path: broker asks for a flyer/reel/post, request goes into a queue, they see it, download, post it
items.evidence: Confirmed by direct parse, not by doc: `python3 -c "json.load(open('vercel.json'))['crons']"` returns exactly 49 entries and marketing-inbox-poll is not among them, while app/api/cron/marketing-inbox-poll/route.ts:9 states 'Schedule: every 2 minutes — wired in vercel.json'. The route itself is complete (requireCronAuth then pollMarketingInbox). app/marketing/request/page.tsx:1-12 documents itself as no-auth, no-backend-writes, mailto-only, and page.tsx:32 only reads session/identity to pin dynamic rendering. The page is linked from lib/marketing-brain/inbox-reply.ts:63 (the reply signature), so brokers can reach it — but nothing in the admin nav points to it. app/dashboard/marketing/inbox/page.tsx is the only queue view.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] The auditor got this right and I confirmed the cron absence by parsing vercel.json rather than grepping. Additional detail they missed: /marketing/request is reachable only via an emailed link — it appears in no nav and no dashboard, so a broker who did not keep the email cannot find it. The intake pipeline is therefore dark at both ends: no cron to consume requests, and no in-product entry point to create them.
items.why_it_matters: A broker emailing marketing@ryan-realty.com today gets silence. That is the single worst first impression for a recruiting pitch built on marketing support.

items.requirement: Producers substitute the correct listing agent's headshot, name, phone, email into every branded deliverable
items.evidence: Confirmed line by line. scripts/build_property_feature_sheet.mjs:47-66 carries a real BROKERS registry (name, role, phone, web, headshot path, email aliases) and resolveAgent() matches by token then by email, warning and defaulting to Matt only when unresolved. scripts/build_listing_reveal.py:79-81 renders `draw_centered(draw, "541.213.6706", phone_fnt, NAVY, ...)` — Matt's phone baked into the image, with no agent parameter anywhere in the file. grep for ListAgentEmail / resolveListingAgent across listing_video_v4/src and listing_video_v4/scripts returns only unrelated news-clip and email-send matches — the Remotion pipeline has no agent-resolution code, contradicting the 'Listing-agent rule' asserted in CLAUDE.md.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Auditor was accurate here and this is the item where CLAUDE.md most clearly lies about the code. Worth adding: the working registry in build_property_feature_sheet.mjs hardcodes each broker's phone in a fourth location (after lib/admin.ts, lib/crm/constants.ts, and getBrokers.ts alias map), so a fourth broker means editing at least four files across two languages.
items.why_it_matters: Handing a recruited broker a flyer with the owner's phone number on it is worse than handing them nothing.

items.requirement: Broker onboarding: Google Workspace email/account provisioning + system access
items.evidence: The DB half IS self-service UI, which the auditor denied. app/admin/(protected)/brokers/page.tsx:29-38 renders an 'Add broker' button to /admin/brokers/new (page exists) and a 'Roles & permissions' link to /admin/crm/settings/team (page exists), both superuser-only. app/actions/admin-roles.ts exports upsertAdminRole/removeAdminRole server actions, and app/components/admin/AdminUsersList.tsx:13-15 notes the admin_roles manager was consolidated onto those same actions. What is not automated: Google Workspace account creation (lib/google-calendar.ts documents DWD impersonation of existing mailboxes only; docs/install-kits/paul-email-signature/README.md walks a human through admin.google.com), and the hardcoded identity maps (lib/crm/constants.ts:15-19, lib/data/brokers/getBrokers.ts:118-119 plus its duplicate in app/actions/brokers.ts) which require a code change and deploy.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor claimed onboarding requires Matt to 'manually insert brokers + admin_roles rows (or write a migration)'. False — both are UI flows today (/admin/brokers/new, /admin/crm/settings/team). The real, sharper gap is that completing those UI steps is NOT sufficient: unless the new broker's login email is also added to CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL in code and deployed, their dashboard fails open and shows them everyone's book. Onboarding is a two-system operation where the code half is invisible to the person doing the UI half.]
items.why_it_matters: The onboarding path looks complete in the UI and silently is not, which is how a recruited broker ends up with a mis-scoped dashboard on day one.

items.evidence: crm-gmail-sync is genuinely scheduled (vercel.json crons: '/api/cron/crm-gmail-sync', '9,24,39,54 * * * *' — confirmed in the parsed 49-entry array), so broker-client email lands in the CRM timeline for after-the-fact human review. Real compliance machinery exists but targets OUTBOUND messaging, not broker email content: lib/crm/suppression-helpers.ts, lib/crm/membership-consent.ts, lib/crm/audience.ts, and a 'settings.compliance' capability (lib/admin/capabilities.ts, superuser-only) covering suppression and block lists. Real supervision exists for transactions: app/admin/(protected)/sign-off/page.tsx renders getPrincipalSignOffQueue with banking-day review deadlines. Nothing anywhere scans broker email content for keywords, fair-housing risk, or advertising-disclosure violations, and no alerting or compliance dashboard reads the synced mail.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor's evidence was one grep and understated what exists — there is substantial compliance and principal-broker-supervision code (TCPA suppression, consent gating, a banking-day sign-off queue), just none of it aimed at email content. Status stays partial for the right reason: supervision infrastructure is real, email-content monitoring is zero.]
items.why_it_matters: Matt is the principal broker and carries license liability for what recruited brokers write to clients. Passive timeline visibility across three brokers does not scale and produces no alert when something goes wrong.

items.requirement: Per-broker performance visibility (own leads, own content results)
items.evidence: lib/admin/capabilities.ts:97-100 sets `'performance.view': []` with an in-file comment stating D3's end state grants brokers a scoped own-book Performance overview 'but that page doesn't exist yet (spec 06)', and that the only Performance surface today is /admin/analytics whose layout is superuser-only, so granting the capability now would dead-end brokers. 'performance.financials', 'financials.view' and 'commissions.view' are likewise [] (superuser-only).
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor did not cover this requirement at all.] A recruited broker cannot see any performance surface — not their lead volume, not their conversion, not their content results, not their own commission rows. The capability is deliberately withheld because the scoped page has not been built.
items.why_it_matters: A recruiting pitch built on 'we market for you' is unprovable to the recruit if they can never see what the marketing produced for them.

items.requirement: Instagram auto-post per broker (eventually — copy/creative only for now)
items.evidence: grep for broker_id / brokerId / broker_slug across app/api/social/ returns zero matches. Publishing runs on one brokerage-wide Meta token against the single locked handle. No per-broker OAuth table, connection flow, or publish route exists anywhere under app/api/social.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Entirely absent, no scaffolding, matching Matt's 'eventually' framing.
items.why_it_matters: Not blocking today, but it is the eventual end state of the self-service pitch and nothing built so far anticipates a second publishing identity.

shared_primitives_needed: Broker identity must move from code to data. Today it lives in at least four hardcoded places — lib/admin.ts:2 (superuser email), lib/crm/constants.ts:15-19 (CRM_BROKER_BY_EMAIL), lib/data/brokers/getBrokers.ts:118-119 (BROKER_SLUG_ALIASES, duplicated in app/actions/brokers.ts), and scripts/build_property_feature_sheet.mjs:53-57 (phones/headshots). One resolver reading public.brokers, consumed by web, CRM, and every producer.

Fail-CLOSED scoping. Every `if (scopeToSelf && crmSlug)` / `if (access.brokerSlug)` in app/actions/broker-command-center.ts (lines 243, 254, 269) and app/actions/crm.ts:1794 must become: unresolved slug on a non-superuser returns an empty result set and logs, never an unfiltered query.

A broker-scoped content queue over marketing_brain_actions that renders inside /admin/broker-dashboard without the isSuperuser gate — and a matching non-empty capability array so /admin/broker-links and a scoped launchpad actually reach brokers ('content.marketing' and 'content.media' are both [] in lib/admin/capabilities.ts:130-131).

A branded-deliverable record type. data/asset-library/manifest.json and the media tables store source assets only; nothing models 'this finished flyer, rendered for broker X'. Until that exists, no gallery can show a broker their own branded content.
A mechanical gate asserting every route whose docstring claims a schedule appears in vercel.json's crons array. marketing-inbox-poll drifted, was caught by a one-off audit, and is still dark.

An authz gate asserting every page under a nav-hidden capability also carries an in-page guard — app/admin/(protected)/media/photos/page.tsx is nav-gated by 'content.media' (superuser) but has no page-level check.
open_questions_for_owner: Have Paul's and Rebecca's admin_roles rows actually been updated from the migration's placeholder emails (rebecca.peterson@, paul.stevenson@) to their real Google logins (rebeccapeterson@, paul@)? If not, they cannot log in at all. If they were updated to something else, they are currently seeing the whole company's client and task list via the fail-open filters.
Should /admin/broker-links simply be unlocked for broker-role users (one edit to CAPABILITY_ROLES), and if so should each broker see only their own row or the whole team's links?
Is the Marketing launchpad's superuser gate an intentional quality control while the brand-voice gates mature, or leftover from before broker roles existed?
Is marketing-inbox-poll unregistered by oversight, or deliberately parked over cost or distrust of the Haiku dispatch? It is the only intake path and it is currently silent.

How is tc_deals.broker_name written, and does it match the full legal display names seeded in public.brokers ('Paul Michael Stevenson')? If not, every non-superuser broker's Deals section is silently empty.

Do you want compliance monitoring on broker email content (keyword/fair-housing/advertising-disclosure scanning with alerts to you as principal broker), or is timeline review sufficient at three brokers — and does that answer change at six?
